regulation-optimality literature (L3 read): cost of needless enzyme synthesis vs cost of missing substrate; optimal regulation as threshold policy on anticipated flux; predictive regulation and its forecast cost
donor_structure: A cell deciding whether to synthesize an enzyme faces: irreversible synthesis cost (amino acids, energy, burden), uncertain future substrate availability, and a threshold regulation policy (induction only when the substrate signal clears a margin above synthesis breakeven). Comparative statics from regulation-optimality analysis: optimal induction strictness INCREASES with environmental volatility; catabolite repression implements global gating across parallel options; induction lag is the price of responsiveness. Predictive (anticipatory) regulation commits before evidence and pays a forecast cost.
target_structure: A_T11 at R5 (same target as A6-R1): module promotion under uncertain future use, vi-fixed-ecology removed. This receipt supplies the INDEPENDENT second-partition derivation of the promotion gate.
